dish: Teochew boneless braised duck rice / kway teow / porridge
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-04, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020
w: Ghim Moh's Michelin Bib Gourmand duck stall: boneless Teochew-style braised duck over rice, kway teow or congee, dressed in a dark herbal gravy whose braising stock is reused and replenished daily — a $3-$5 bowl with years of depth in it.

dish: Chwee kueh — steamed rice cakes with charcoal-fried chye poh
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-54, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020
w: A household name since 1959 and a Michelin Guide pick: soft-but-springy steamed rice cakes (minimum four) heaped with chye poh fried over a charcoal stove, which gives the preserved radish a smokier depth than the gas-cooked norm.

n: Guan Kee Fried Kway Teow — CLOSED
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020
w: Started in 1969 and at Ghim Moh since 1978, this was one of Singapore's most-queued char kway teow stalls (Bib Gourmand 2019) — it closed for good on 28 Nov 2023 when its 77-year-old owner retired after fainting at the wok. Kept here as a flagged closure.

dish: Chai tow kway (fried carrot cake), black or white, chye poh made in-house
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-16, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020
w: The most popular carrot cake at Ghim Moh — a family stall that makes both the radish cake and the chye poh from scratch daily; the queue starts at 6:30am and limited portions sell out, rewarding early birds with strong wok hei.

dish: Wok-hei beef hor fun (brown gravy); prawn / sliced-fish hor fun (clear gravy)
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-44, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020
w: Fried to order over a superheated wok so the flat rice noodles take on real wok hei before the gravy goes in — the brown-sauce beef hor fun is the bestseller; written up by Dr Leslie Tay and Miss Tam Chiak and tested by Seth Lui as one of Singapore's best-rated hor fun.

dish: Appam with orange sugar & coconut; 'Princess' appam; Royal thosai; putu mayam
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-26, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020
w: Formerly Heavens Indian Curry, now a mother-and-son appam and thosai specialist: lacy-edged, pillow-centred fermented-rice appam with grated coconut and orange sugar, or the indulgent 'Princess' crowned with butter, cheddar and a fried egg.

dish: Charcoal claypot rice with chicken, lap cheong & salted fish
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-19, 44 Holland Drive, S270044
w: Holland Drive's headline stall and a Michelin Bib Gourmand year after year (incl. 2024 and 2025): every claypot is cooked from scratch over charcoal, so the grains stay separate with a crackling crust — call ahead, because the wait can run to an hour.

dish: Teochew kway chap & thinly sliced braised duck
n: Cheng Heng Kway Chap and Braised Duck Rice
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-05, 44 Holland Drive, S270044
w: A Michelin-recognised kway chap (Michelin Plate, 2018) where the broad rice sheets swim in a herbal soy broth beside braised pork and innards, plus the stall's famous finely sliced braised duck — expect a 30-minute morning queue.

dish: Breakfast lontong / mee rebus; afternoon nasi padang (mutton rendang, sambal)
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-12, 44 Holland Drive, S270044
w: The Malay stall at Holland Drive that tastes like someone's mum cooked it — creamy coconut lontong and mee soto in the morning, then a changing nasi padang spread (rendang, petai, curry chicken) that sells out early.

dish: Hakka noodles loaded with yong tau foo and fried wantons
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-15, 44 Holland Drive, S270044
w: One of Holland Drive's busier stalls: springy Hakka noodles heaped with yong tau foo pieces and crisp fried wantons — a generous neighbourhood bowl.
